what_it_does: Training a large AI model can take weeks on hundreds of GPUs, and machines fail — especially cheap 'spot' cloud machines that can be interrupted at any time. To survive failures, teams periodically save a snapshot (called a checkpoint) of all the model's learned numbers to durable storage like a hard drive. The problem is a dilemma: save checkpoints rarely and you lose hours of work when a machine fails; save them often and the saving process itself slows training down. PCcheck resolves this by running the save operation in the background at the same time as training continues, so the GPU never has to stop working. It uses a technique called copy-on-write — making a frozen copy of the model's numbers at a specific moment without stopping the GPU — and then streams that frozen copy to storage in stages while the GPU continues learning. The system carefully tracks which snapshot is complete and valid so it can always recover to a clean state.
